Jessica the jackrabbit wants to climb down a wall. The wall consists of 2026 horizontal layers stacked vertically. The $n$th layer from the top is partitioned into $2^n - 1$ identical rectangular bricks arranged side by side. Jessica begins in the topmost layer, which contains a single brick. A move consists of Jessica going down one layer to a brick that shares a side with the brick she is currently on.

Determine, with proof, the total number of distinct sequences of moves Jessica can take to reach the 2026th layer.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let the common width of the wall be \(1\). Suppose some layer has \(m\) bricks. Since the next layer has
\[
2^{n+1}-1=2(2^n-1)+1=2m+1
\]
bricks, number the bricks in each layer from left to right.

The \(i\)-th brick in the layer with \(m\) bricks spans the horizontal interval
\[
\left(\frac{i-1}{m},\frac{i}{m}\right).
\]
The \(j\)-th brick in the layer below spans
\[
\left(\frac{j-1}{2m+1},\frac{j}{2m+1}\right).
\]
They share a side exactly when these intervals overlap with positive length:
\[
\frac{i-1}{m}<\frac{j}{2m+1}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{j-1}{2m+1}<\frac{i}{m}.
\]

These become
\[
j>2i-2+\frac{i-1}{m}
\quad\text{and}\quad
j<2i+1+\frac{i}{m}.
\]
Since \(1\le i\le m\),
\[
2i-2\le 2i-2+\frac{i-1}{m}<2i-1,
\]
and
\[
2i+1<2i+1+\frac{i}{m}\le 2i+2.
\]
Thus the only integers \(j\) satisfying both inequalities are
\[
j=2i-1,\quad 2i,\quad 2i+1.
\]
So every brick has exactly \(3\) possible bricks to move down to.

There are \(2025\) moves from the top layer to the 2026th layer, and each move has exactly \(3\) choices. Hence the total number of distinct sequences of moves is
\[
\boxed{3^{2025}}.
\]
